title: A separated Noetherian scheme of dimension zero is affine
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension $\dim Y\le 0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], including $Y=\varnothing$. Then $Y$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. In particular the trivial invertible module $\mathcal O_Y$ [def-sc-invertible-module] is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete directly, including the empty scheme. Install the resulting Finite Y and DiscreteTopology Y instances.
Apply the proved Mathlib finite-discrete scheme affineness instance (lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine). Quasi-compactness and separatedness are not needed for this step.

Unfold IsAmple. Compactness is assumed. For each point choose n=1 and the global section obtained by transporting 1 through the inverse right unitor from the structure module to its tensor power one, and choose U=top, affine by step 2. Construct the canonical additive map from the structure-module stalk to the local ring as a colimit desc of the ring germs; germ compatibility with scalar multiplication makes it linear using stalkLinearMapMk. Compose it with the linear stalk map of the right unitor. This composite sends the chosen germ to 1, by naturality of germs and the inverse-hom identity. Its image of the maximal ideal times the source stalk is contained in the maximal ideal. Membership of the chosen germ there would therefore give 1 in the maximal ideal, contradicting maximality. This proves that the nonvanishing locus is the top open.
